summary: Focused Phase 2 (TEXT->UUID, ~75 columns / 22 tables / 39 FKs / 21 RLS policies) regression. Ran the 78-test suite tests/test_iter108_uuid_migration_regression.py (schema invariants, auth for all 4 roles incl. MFA, dashboard, meetings CRUD+cascade delete, org structure/settings/teams/invites, recording lifecycle, review edits+comments+audit+signoff/reopen, prep, schedules, admin, portfolio, super-admin, scoped-manager, template, rescan, plus 5 dedicated cross-org RLS isolation tests) and a Playwright pass as admin (cookie-injected) + attendee (real UI login) over Dashboard, Organisation People/Structure, Settings, Schedules, Admin Library, Team Themes, New Meeting create, Dashboard delete-meeting, My Portfolio. Result: 70/78 backend tests green. RLS isolation is CLEAN (zero foreign-org rows visible at both API and db-role level, empty org context fails closed, cross-org write denied). Org structure page (the endpoint that broke twice) now renders settings/teams/unassigned staff correctly. Meeting create/delete-cascade, review sign-off/reopen, schedules, team/setting creation, admin users, dashboard all pass. 4 genuine UUID-migration defects remain, 2 of them user-facing on every load.

critical.issue: 500 asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidTextRepresentationError: invalid input syntax for type uuid: "supervision_template:b00bf04f-...". init_db.py Phase 2 converted settings.id to UUID (id_columns list line ~825: ARRAY['settings','id']) but that column is a COMPOSITE STRING KEY, not a uuid — admin.py:484/501, review.py:1270 and utils/transcription_pipeline.py:262 all key rows as f"supervision_template:{org_id}". Same class of key that was correctly EXCLUDED for login_attempts.identifier. Impact: (a) Settings -> Supervision Template tab shows red 'Failed to load settings. Please refresh.' banner on every load, template cannot be read or saved; (b) backend log: 'Rescan failed for meeting c20802af...: invalid input syntax for type uuid'; (c) AI analysis pipeline can no longer load the org supervision template. Also a DEPLOYMENT LANDMINE: settings.id is NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, so on any environment where the settings table is non-empty, migration step 4 (UPDATE %I SET %I = NULL WHERE ... !~ uuid-regex) raises a not-null violation and the whole DO block silently rolls back (only a RAISE WARNING) -> prod would keep TEXT columns while code assumes UUID. Fix: remove ARRAY['settings','id'] (and probably ARRAY['settings','org_id'] is fine) from id_columns, revert settings.id to TEXT, and make step 4 refuse to NULL a column that participates in a primary key instead of doing it silently.

500 asyncpg.exceptions.UndefinedFunctionError: operator does not exist: text = uuid (traceback: routers/portfolio.py line 299 get_portfolio -> line 114 _build_portfolio_data). The same bind param $2 is used against a uuid column AND a jsonb text expression in one query: `sign_off_manager_id != $2` (uuid) together with `elem->>'user_id' = $2` (text) — Postgres resolves $2 as uuid, so the text comparison fails. Impact: 'My Portfolio' page is broken for EVERY user; UI renders the misleading message 'Portfolio not found' (masking a 500) and PDF export 500s. Fix: `elem->>'user_id' = $2::text` (the pattern already used correctly in meetings.py:297 `created_by::text = ANY($1)`). Same bug at portfolio.py:128.

500 operator does not exist: text = uuid — routers/admin.py:1420-1428. One param $1 (scoped_ids) is compared to created_by/sign_off_manager_id (uuid) AND to a->>'user_id' (text). Org-level admins/managers take the else-branch so this only 500s for managers with a team/setting scope. Fix: `created_by = ANY($1::uuid[]) OR sign_off_manager_id = ANY($1::uuid[]) OR ... a->>'user_id' = ANY($1::text[])`.

500 operator does not exist: text = uuid — routers/admin.py:1494 (SEC-002 scope clause, same mixed uuid/text param as meetings-brief). Scoped managers cannot export evidence at all. Fix: separate ::uuid[] / ::text[] casts.

minor.endpoint: GET /api/meetings/{meeting_id} (and any /{id} route) with a non-UUID path segment
minor.issue: GET /api/meetings/not-a-uuid returns 500 (asyncpg InvalidTextRepresentationError: invalid input syntax for type uuid: "not-a-uuid") instead of 404/422. Pre-migration this was a clean 404. Recommend typing the path params as uuid.UUID in FastAPI (auto 422) or validating before query — otherwise every id route is a trivially reachable 500 for any bot/typo.

rca_of_the_issue: Two independent root causes. (1) settings.id was wrongly included in the Phase 2 TEXT->UUID column list even though the application uses composite string primary keys ('supervision_template:{org_id}') for that table (admin.py:484/501, review.py:1270, transcription_pipeline.py:262). Every read/write now aborts at bind time with 'invalid input syntax for type uuid'. In this preview env the table happened to be empty (0 rows) so the ALTER succeeded; on any environment with rows, migration step 4's blanket `SET col = NULL WHERE col !~ uuid_regex` would violate the NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY and roll the whole DO block back with only a warning — silently leaving the schema on TEXT. (2) Several queries bind one parameter to both a now-UUID column and a jsonb `->>` text expression (portfolio.py:118/128, admin.py:1428, admin.py:1485). Postgres infers the param type from the uuid comparison, so the text comparison fails with 'operator does not exist: text = uuid'. Before the migration both sides were TEXT so a single param worked. Reproduction: GET /api/admin/template (500), GET /api/portfolio/831bdaef-14ca-49ed-8fb0-9b8d36bc1ef6 (500), and, as a manager whose scope is team-level, GET /api/admin/meetings-brief and POST /api/admin/export-evidence (500). Mitigation: exclude settings.id from the migration (revert to TEXT) and add explicit per-side casts (::uuid[] / ::text[] / ::text) to the mixed-type predicates.
